As Panagbenga Festival paints Baguio City in full bloom, expect vibrant parades, heavier traffic, and thousands of happy festival goers filling the streets. 🌼✨

Here’s your quick guide before heading out:

🚧 Road Closures
Major roads like Session Road, Harrison Road, and Magsaysay Road will have early morning closures during parade days. Plan ahead and leave early.

🚶 Best Way Around the CBD
Once you’re in the city center, walking is your best friend. Wear comfy shoes, stay hydrated, and enjoy the street energy.

🧭 Pro Tip for Foodies
When the crowd gets overwhelming and your feet need a break, step away from the noise and recharge with a feast that’s just as festive.

At Myeongdong Jjigae, the flavors are blooming too. 🌸🔥 From unlimited samgyup (with unlimited cheese!) to comforting buffet options or hotpot, it’s the perfect pause between parades. Refuel, cool down, and get back to the celebration energized.

📍 2F City Hub, 92 Gen. Luna Rd (Corner Leonard Wood), Baguio City
🕥 10:30 AM – 9:00 PM

Celebrate the colors outside. Taste the bloom inside.

We understand na safety should always be the priority, pero paano naman yung ibang contingents from different provinces who also gave so much effort, time, and sacrifice?
Tiniis namin yung sobrang haba ng parade at yung init ng grass. Sugat-sugat na yung tuhod at paa namin, puro paltos na, and sobrang sakit na ng katawan—but we still chose to continue and finish our performance. Hindi man namin na-perfect yung routine because super init na ng grass and it was already 12:00 PM, we still gave our 101%.

And why did we perform 4th when we were set to be 6th? The program was unorganized, and felt cooked. It was unacceptable and disappointing.

This is not about insecurity or anything. We just want to be enlightened kung ano talaga ang nangyari and how the title was awarded. We’re simply asking for a fair and clear explanation.

Still, thank you Panagbenga 2026. Despite the flaws, we enjoyed and celebrated.

Disappointed but grateful, we remain proud of our performance. ☝🏻✨

PANANG CURRY 🥘🌶️🇹🇭

a regional variation of the typical Thai red curry originating from central Thailand and it is also one of my new favorites. 
 
Feel free to substitute the protein with whatever you would like. Shrimp, beef, pork, fish, tofu if your vegetarian. It all works. 

If you have the time on your hands you could make your own curry paste but im using pre made paste to make it easier. 

Ingredients:

1.5 boneless chicken thighs
8oz coconut milk
Palm or block cane sugar to taste
Fish sauce to taste
2tbsp Store bought panang curry paste (mae ploy)
6-7 Kaffir lime leaves
Thai chilis to taste

Optional:
1 red bell pepper

The curry paste does already have salt in it so depending on how much you use you may not need that much fish sauce. Give it a taste before you add anything extra.

History of Panagbenga Festival

The Panagbenga Festival, also known as the Baguio Flower Festival, began in 1995 as a symbol of hope and recovery after the 1990 Luzon earthquake. The word “Panagbenga” comes from the Kankanaey term meaning “season of blooming,” representing renewal, unity, and resilience.

Held every February in Baguio City, this month-long celebration showcases grand floral floats, lively street dancing inspired by Cordillera culture, and the natural beauty that made Baguio the Summer Capital of the Philippines. 🌼🏔️

More than just flowers, Panagbenga is a tribute to the creativity of the Cordilleran people and the city’s journey of rising stronger together.
